threads.summary: nats-container record is written before the port asserts and ensure_nats can refuse, so a refused up.sh leaves a record naming a container that does not exist; down.sh then never falls back to legion-smoke-nats (legacy rig re-run on its own SMOKE_DIR orphans the legacy container) and a same-SMOKE_DIR/different-SMOKE_PROJECT mistake overwrites a live rig's record. Fix: write the record after ensure_nats returns; add an assertion to the existing refusal case that the record is absent after refusal.
'naming the container and both ports' overstates ensure_nats's message, which names the container and the configured port only; fix wording or print docker port's mapping.

keyFindings.description: Record written before any refusal point (port asserts 580-585, ensure_nats 592). Reproduced with a fake docker: no record -> down.sh falls back and removes legion-smoke-nats; record left by a refused start -> down.sh inspects only legion-smoke-nats-<slug>, removes nothing. thermonuclear-deep-review reproduced independently with a sourced-up.sh driver refused at ensure_nats. Proposed fix (move the write after ensure_nats) run against up.test.sh in a temp copy: 18 PASS.
Docs claim the port-mismatch refusal names both ports; the message names the container and the configured port.
Comment states the incident (first rig killed at boot) rather than the invariant (the daemon binds port+1).
New shellcheck SC2154 (false positive via source=/dev/null) and two SC2329 infos on changed lines; implementer handoff's 'none on changed lines' inaccurate.
sjawhar/24 assertions depend on the last main() case having run as sjawhar/24; make the block self-contained.
-e then $(<record): an unreadable/directory record aborts down.sh under set -e after processes are stopped; -r would treat it as malformed.
worker_stream_port resolves YAML > LEGION_WORKER_STREAM_PORT env > port+1 and the daemon inherits the operator env; optional: pin worker_stream_port in the generated legion.yaml.

That rig's daemon (pid 1741820, port 19391), listener, bridge, container legion16-smoke-nats, and pid files were untouched. The subagent was told to run no real rig script again.
